_comment: PostToolUse guard fired after Agent/Task returns. It has NO deny path: it never prints a
decision, it always exits 0 on a parseable payload, and its entire observable behavior is one
side effect — writing the flag file that the PreToolUse counterpart later reads to block
Read/Grep on non-.planning paths. So the branch a broken port would silently destroy is not a
'deny' string, it is the FLAG FILE'S PATH. If the port writes it under a different name, the
PreToolUse guard never finds it and simply stops guarding.
The flag lands in tempfile.gettempdir(), which is outside the harness's cwd snapshot and would
therefore be invisible. Every case sets TMPDIR='.' so gettempdir() resolves to the sandbox cwd
and the write shows up in the filesystem delta. Verified against the Python original: with

cases.name: task-returned-writes-session-flag
cases._comment: Main path. Silence + exit 0 is how a PostToolUse hook says 'carry on'; the real output is the flag file. Pins the exact filename ds-workflow-flags/subagent-returned-<CLAUDE_SESSION_ID> and its contents ('1'). Verified: exit 0, empty stdout, ./ds-workflow-flags/subagent-returned-sess-abc-33a386c9464a4538527687ee331d081d created.
cases._tsComment: TS-ONLY EXPECTATION. `sessionFlagKey` now appends a digest of the RAW session id, because deleting disallowed characters was not injective: "sess/one", "sess#one", "sess one", and "sessone" all collapsed to one key, so distinct sessions shared a flag file — the very cross-session leak this key was introduced to stop. Python still names the file after CLAUDE_SESSION_ID verbatim, so the two sides legitimately diverge and the TS side is pinned exactly: stdout hash, exit code, and the full filesystem delta.

cases.name: payload-session-id-outranks-an-empty-env-var
cases._comment: NEW CONTRACT, deliberately diverging from the Python original. The flag key came from process.env.CLAUDE_SESSION_ID, which Claude Code never sets, so all three DS flag hooks resolved to the literal 'default' and every concurrent session shared one flag file. The key now comes from the payload's session_id, which is present on every event these hooks are wired to. Python still reads the env var, so tsExpected pins the TS side exactly: complete stdout hash, exit code, and the full filesystem delta.

cases.name: stale-flag-truncated-not-appended
cases._comment: Second subagent return in the same session: the flag dir already exists (os.makedirs exist_ok=True must not raise) and the flag file already holds stale content. open(...,'w') truncates, so the result is exactly '1'. A port that appends, or that skips the write when the file exists, diverges here. Verified: exit 0, content becomes '1', no error from the pre-existing directory.

cases.name: non-object-payload-exits-1-without-flag
cases._comment: Malformed-payload branch: the hook dies before reaching the write, so exit 1, empty stdout, NO flag file. The harness JSON-stringifies `stdin`, so a bare string arrives as the valid JSON document "not json"; json.loads() succeeds and the crash lands one line later on tool_input.get -> AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'get'. Same observable outcome as a true parse error, and it is the only way to reach this branch through the harness (see notes). It matters because it is the one case where the guard legitimately leaves NO flag: a port that defensively coerces a non-object payload to {} would write the flag anyway and wrongly arm the PreToolUse blocker. Verified: exit 1, empty stdout, zero filesystem delta.
